devlin2019.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
devlin2019.abstract: We introduce BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.
devlin2019.full_text:
ABSTRACT: We introduce BERT, a new language representation model which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers.

INTRODUCTION: Language model pre-training has been shown to be effective for improving many natural language processing tasks.

RESULTS: Table 1 shows our results on the GLUE benchmark. BERT-Large achieves 93.2% accuracy on the overall GLUE score, establishing a new state-of-the-art across all tasks. This represents a significant improvement over previous work.

CONCLUSION: We have introduced BERT and shown its effectiveness for a wide range of NLP tasks through extensive experiments.

brown2020.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
brown2020.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated substantial gains on many NLP tasks through pre-training on large corpora followed by fine-tuning. We show that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance. We train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters.
brown2020.full_text:
ABSTRACT: We train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, 10x more than any previous non-sparse language model.

INTRODUCTION: We demonstrate that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, sometimes even reaching competitiveness with prior state-of-the-art fine-tuning approaches.

MODEL: GPT-3 has 175 billion parameters and was trained on diverse internet text including Common Crawl, WebText2, Books1, Books2, and Wikipedia.

RESULTS: GPT-3 achieves strong performance on many NLP datasets in the few-shot learning setting.

vaswani2017.title: Attention is All You Need
vaswani2017.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. We propose a new architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
vaswani2017.full_text:
ABSTRACT: We propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.

INTRODUCTION: Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output sequences, which inherently sequential nature precludes parallelization.

MODEL ARCHITECTURE: The Transformer uses stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both encoder and decoder. Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces.

RESULTS: Our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks.

he2016.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
he2016.abstract: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions.
he2016.full_text:
ABSTRACT: We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously.

INTRODUCTION: Deep networks naturally integrate low/mid/high-level features and classifiers in an end-to-end multi-layer fashion.

RESULTS: We evaluate our approach on ImageNet 2015 classification challenge. Our 152-layer ResNet achieves 3.57% top-5 error rate on the ImageNet test set, winning first place in the ILSVRC 2015 classification competition.

CONCLUSION: The residual learning principle is generic and applicable to various vision recognition tasks.

srivastava2014.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
srivastava2014.abstract: Deep neural nets with a large number of parameters are very powerful machine learning systems. However, overfitting is a serious problem in such networks. Large networks are also slow to use. Dropout is a technique for addressing this problem.
srivastava2014.full_text:
ABSTRACT: We propose dropout, a simple and effective technique for preventing overfitting in neural networks.

INTRODUCTION: With dropout, neural network units are randomly dropped along with their connections during training. This prevents units from co-adapting too much.

METHOD: During training, dropout samples from an exponential number of different thinned networks. At test time, we use a single unthinned network with weighted connections to approximate the effect of averaging the predictions of all the thinned networks.

RESULTS: Dropout improves the performance of neural networks on supervised learning tasks in vision, speech recognition, document classification, and computational biology.

ground_truth.reasoning: Paper explicitly states 'BERT-Large achieves 93.2% accuracy on the overall GLUE score' in the Results section.
Paper states GPT-3 has 175 billion parameters, NOT over 200 billion. This is an overclaim.
Paper explicitly describes Transformer as 'relying entirely on an attention mechanism' and details self-attention in the Model Architecture section.
Paper states 3.57% top-5 error rate, not 3.6%. Very close (rounding) but not exact match. Mostly supported.
Paper clearly states 'neural network units are randomly dropped during training' to prevent overfitting.
